findings.title: DMARC not enforced (p=none): domain can be spoofed for BEC/wire fraud
findings.deal_impact: Domain can be spoofed for BEC/wire fraud targeting customers and finance counterparties in fleet SaaS operations; diligence should confirm DMARC enforcement roadmap and monitoring before close.

remediation.summary: Move DMARC from p=none to quarantine then reject, validating all legitimate senders and rua reporting first.

findings.title: SPF uses soft/neutral fail
findings.deal_impact: Soft-fail SPF weakens anti-spoofing controls and compounds DMARC non-enforcement risk for payment and customer communications.

remediation.summary: Inventory authorized senders, then change SPF qualifier from ~all to -all in coordination with DMARC enforcement.

findings.title: DNSSEC not enabled
findings.deal_impact: Unsigned DNS increases cache-poisoning/redirection risk, though exploitability is lower than email and edge findings; relevant to insurability hygiene.

remediation.summary: Enable DNSSEC at registrar/registry and monitor DS/DNSKEY validation.

findings.title: Publicly logged hostnames suggest exposed admin/legacy/staging systems

evidence.excerpt: risky hostname pattern=vpn, first_seen=2023-02-11, last_seen=2026-09-30; risky_hostnames_count=4

findings.deal_impact: Public CT names suggest VPN, legacy CI, staging API and legacy portal attack surface that may lack production hardening; validate ownership, authentication and decommissioning in diligence.

remediation.summary: Validate each risky hostname, restrict admin/staging access behind MFA/VPN, patch or decommission legacy systems, and inventory certificates.

findings.title: Large certificate footprint relative to company size
findings.deal_impact: 47 hostnames for a 201-1000 employee company suggests surface sprawl that may complicate asset inventory and patch accountability.

remediation.summary: Reconcile the 47 CT hostnames against CMDB/cloud inventories, assign owners, and remove stale certificates/hosts.

findings.title: Deprecated TLS versions offered

evidence.excerpt: tls_support TLSv1.0=true, TLSv1.1=true, TLSv1.2=true; tls_versions=[TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1, TLSv1.2], status_code=200

findings.deal_impact: Deprecated TLS on www weakens transport security for customer sessions and may signal uneven edge configuration management versus the apex host.

remediation.summary: Disable TLSv1.0 and TLSv1.1 on www and all edge endpoints, retaining TLSv1.2+ with modern ciphers.

findings.title: HSTS not set

evidence.excerpt: headers strict-transport-security=null, content-security-policy=null, x-frame-options=SAMEORIGIN, server=nginx; status_code=200

findings.deal_impact: Missing HSTS allows SSL-stripping/downgrade risk on first visits and indicates basic header hygiene gaps for underwriting.

remediation.summary: Set Strict-Transport-Security with an appropriate max-age on apex and www after confirming all subdomains are HTTPS-ready.

findings.title: Internet-facing appliance listed in CISA KEV (version not verified)

evidence.excerpt: Potential exposure: CVE-PLACEHOLDER-0001, vendor=ExampleGate, product=ExampleGate SSL-VPN, matched_fingerprint version=7.0.11, kind=appliance, host=www.brightwaterfleet.example, match_tier=appliance_exposed, match_level=product; KEV lists products, not affected versions; version not verified. kev_snapshot_date=2026-10-20

findings.deal_impact: Potential exposure of an internet-facing SSL-VPN appliance with a KEV-listed product could enable remote intrusion; version is not verified, so urgent confirmation of patch level and exposure is a pre-close diligence item.

remediation.summary: Immediately verify ExampleGate SSL-VPN version and KEV CVE applicability, patch or isolate the appliance, enforce MFA, and review logs for exploitation.

findings.title: Publicly disclosed security incident in the last 24 months

evidence.excerpt: type=state_ag_breach_notice, date=2025-08-14: Notice filed for unauthorized access to a customer support system; approx. 3,100 individuals notified. Entity match exact; disclosed_within_months=14.

findings.deal_impact: A breach disclosed 14 months ago affecting a customer support system raises regulatory, notification-cost and customer-trust questions; obtain root-cause, closure and remediation evidence in diligence.

remediation.summary: Request incident postmortem, regulator closure status, affected-system remediation, and evidence of post-incident monitoring and control improvements.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in logical access controls (CC6.1)

evidence.excerpt: 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA. These were service-desk accounts created via a legacy provisioning script that bypassed the conditional access policy.

findings.deal_impact: 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA. These were service-desk accounts created via a legacy provisioning script that bypassed the conditional access policy.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC6.1 exception: 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA.

evidence.excerpt: 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days respectively.

findings.deal_impact: 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days respectively.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC6.2 exception: 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days respectively.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in security monitoring (CC7.2)

evidence.excerpt: For 2 consecutive weeks (Nov 10–23, 2025), alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed.

findings.deal_impact: For 2 consecutive weeks (Nov 10–23, 2025), alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC7.2 exception: For 2 consecutive weeks (Nov 10–23, 2025), alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in change management (CC8.1)

evidence.excerpt: 2 of 40 changes lacked documented approval (emergency hotfixes).

findings.deal_impact: 2 of 40 changes lacked documented approval (emergency hotfixes).

remediation.summary: Remediate CC8.1 exception: 2 of 40 changes lacked documented approval (emergency hotfixes).

findings.title: SOC 2 report period ended more than 90 days ago; no bridge letter provided
findings.deal_impact: Report period ended 2026-03-31, 213 days before the assessment date; controls may have changed since.

remediation.summary: Obtain a bridge letter covering through 2026-10-30.

findings.title: Critical subservice organization carved out of SOC 2 scope

evidence.excerpt: Nimbus Cloud Services is carved out of scope: infrastructure hosting; production workloads run in Nimbus Cloud Services (carved out).

findings.deal_impact: Nimbus Cloud Services (infrastructure hosting; production workloads run in Nimbus Cloud Services (carved out)) is carved out of scope and is critical to production or in-scope data.

remediation.summary: Obtain the Nimbus Cloud Services SOC report and assess carve-out risk.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Every admin account is behind MFA. No exceptions. That's been true for years. It's enforced through our conditional access policy.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 testing found 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA because a legacy provisioning script bypassed conditional access, contradicting the no-exceptions claim.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Offboarding is automated. HR flags the termination and access is revoked same day through our identity provider.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 testing found 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days, contradicting same-day automated revocation.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We have a 24 7 SOC through our MSSP, every alert gets looked at, nothing sits. Email

contradictions.explanation: For two consecutive weeks, Nov 10-23, 2025, alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed, contradicting that every alert is looked at.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We're fully locked down there. DMARC is enforced. Nobody can spoof our domain.

contradictions.explanation: The DMARC record is p=none with policy=none, so DMARC is not enforced and the domain can be spoofed.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: No, nothing material. We've never had a breach.

contradictions.explanation: A state AG breach notice dated 2025-08-14 reports unauthorized access to a customer support system and approximately 3,100 individuals notified, contradicting no breach.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We decommissioned the legacy stuff a while back. Everything external goes through the main app and the VPN.

contradictions.explanation: CT log presence alone doesn't prove a host is live; however, legacy-portal and jenkins-old certificates have last_seen dates in Jul-Aug 2026, within 12 months, showing active maintenance and contradicting prior decommissioning.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Annual third party test. The last one came back clean. No highs.

contradictions.explanation: Annual independent penetration testing is corroborated, but the test reported 2 high-severity findings, contradicting the claim that the last test came back clean with no highs.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Daily backups to immutable storage in a second region and we do a restore test every quarter.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 control A1.2-01 was tested with no exceptions and states production data is backed up daily to immutable storage with quarterly restore tests, supporting the claim.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We can get one. one we haven't needed it so far.

contradictions.explanation: Section 5 states management plans to obtain a bridge letter covering April 1, 2026 forward upon request, corroborating that one can be obtained.

deal_recommendations.text: Make signing conditional on verification of the internet-facing appliance version and applicability of the listed exposure, completion of a compromise assessment, and bring-down of security representations, with this work completed in Days 0–30 [F-008].

Commission an independent review, scoped in Days 0–30, that examines the listed appliance exposure and independently validates management representations before reliance is placed on them [F-008] [C-001] [C-002] [C-003] [C-004] [C-005].
Allocate losses arising from the pre-closing incident disclosed on 2025-08-14 through a specific indemnity, while the related postmortem and closure work proceeds in Days 31–60 [F-009].

Expect the disclosed incident to be treated as a known matter likely excluded from representations and warranties coverage, and plan on that basis during the Days 31–60 incident-review window [F-009].

Confirm insurability and likely cyber insurance underwriting requirements before close, addressing the email authentication and access-control matters scheduled for Days 31–60 [F-001] [F-010] [F-011].

Require completion after close of the outstanding access-control, monitoring, change-management, email-authentication, hostname, transport-security, incident, and reporting remediation, tracked across Days 31–60 and Days 61–100 [F-010] [F-011] [F-012] [F-013] [F-001] [F-002] [F-004] [F-006] [F-009] [F-014].
On price, no adjustment is warranted, because total remediation of $142K–$643K across Days 0–30 through After day 100 is immaterial relative to the 50M-250M revenue band [F-008] [F-009].

narrative.executive_summary: Bottom line: Escalate: full cyber diligence required before signing. Brightwater Fleet Systems, Inc. scores 57.3 with a D rating, capped by a critical, potentially exploitable exposure [F-008], a publicly disclosed incident within 24 months [F-009], and multiple management statements contradicted by evidence [C-001] [C-005]. Key risks: The internet-facing appliance requires urgent verification because its version is not verified [F-008]. The 2025-08-14 incident affected a customer support system, with approx. 3,100 individuals notified [F-009]. Access testing found 4 of 25 admin accounts not enforced for multifactor authentication and 3 of 15 terminated users retained access for 6, 11, and 19 business days [F-010] [F-011]. Alerts were not reviewed for 2 consecutive weeks [F-012]. Management credibility: Of 9 statements, 7 were contradicted and 2 supported, including on multifactor authentication, offboarding, alert review, domain enforcement, and incident history [C-001] [C-002] [C-003] [C-004] [C-005].
key_questions_for_management: Provide evidence of the appliance version, patch level, exposure, multifactor authentication status, and log review for exploitation [F-008].
Provide the incident postmortem, regulator closure status, and remediation evidence for the customer support system incident disclosed on 2025-08-14 [F-009] [C-005].
Reconcile the statement that every admin account is behind multifactor authentication with the finding that 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced [F-010] [C-001].
Reconcile the statement that offboarding revokes access the same day with the finding that 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days [F-011] [C-002].
Provide evidence that security alerts are now routed, reviewed, and escalated following the 2 consecutive weeks when alerts were not reviewed [F-012] [C-003].
Confirm the roadmap and timeline to enforce domain authentication, including validation of legitimate senders and reporting [F-001] [C-004].
Provide an inventory reconciling the 47 hostnames and the 4 risky hostnames, with ownership, authentication, patching, and decommissioning status for each [F-004] [F-005] [C-006].
Provide the bridge letter covering through 2026-10-30 and the report for the carved-out infrastructure hosting provider [F-014] [F-015].

exceptions.description: 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA.
exceptions.management_response: Management disabled the legacy provisioning script in April 2026 and has begun migrating service-desk accounts to the standard conditional access policy. Migration expected to complete Q3 2026.

exceptions.description: 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days respectively.
exceptions.management_response: Management is evaluating an automated HR-to-IdP de-provisioning integration. Until then, terminations are processed manually by IT upon email notification from HR.

exceptions.description: For 2 consecutive weeks (Nov 10–23, 2025), alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed.
exceptions.management_response: The distribution list was corrected on November 24, 2025. Management has added a weekly check that alert routing is functioning.

exceptions.description: 2 of 40 changes lacked documented approval (emergency hotfixes).
exceptions.management_response: Management has updated the emergency change procedure to require post-deployment approval within 48 hours.
